bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Chinese import dumping and duty absorption in the Indian insoluble sulphur market — Chinese manufacturers, burdened by excess capacities, directed surplus volumes into the Indian market at aggressive prices. An anti-dumping duty of USD 307 per tonne was imposed, but Chinese exporters absorbed the duty by lowering their selling prices ('anti-absorption'), negating the benefit available to domestic manufacturers. The Company applied for and the DGTR has initiated an anti-absorption investigation, and a further anti-dumping duty absorption application was filed in March 2026; both outcomes are pending, so the distortion is unresolved. As India's leading domestic insoluble sulphur manufacturer, OCCL states it 'bore the brunt of this'. [PROVENANCE: this bundle carried only the boilerplate Directors' Report risk-management-policy paragraph; the substantive risk content is back-filled from the Directors' Report OPERATIONS and FUTURE PROSPECTS sections and the Chairman's statement, which were routed to the profile and strategy_outlook bundles.]
- Sulphur raw-material cost inflation and supply concentration in the Gulf — Average sulphur cost rose from Rs 29 per kg to Rs 52 per kg during the year, reflecting geopolitical disruptions across global supply chains. Ongoing Middle East tensions and disruptions in the Strait of Hormuz have curtailed sulphur availability and disrupted shipping routes and logistics; nearly 45-50% of global sulphur exports originate from Gulf countries, so the industry remains highly vulnerable, and this has resulted in an 80%-100% rise in prices of sulphur and oil. The Company is securing raw materials from various sources, even at a premium, and has raised inventory. [Back-filled from profile / strategy_outlook bundles.]
- Margin compression - realisations cannot keep pace with input costs — Sulphur prices remained elevated while pricing flexibility in the insoluble sulphur market stayed constrained amid intense global competition, so cost pressures moved faster than realisations across parts of the market. Insoluble sulphur realisations could not increase in proportion to the rise in input costs, resulting in margin compression; profitability in FY26 was supported by the sulphuric acid business rather than the flagship product. Energy, freight and insurance costs have also risen sharply and are expected to adversely impact the business. [Back-filled from profile / strategy_outlook bundles.]
- Demand destruction from historically high input costs — Management explicitly flags that 'the historically high input costs may result in demand destruction, which could negatively affect our sales volumes going forward'. Sales volume was already flat during FY26. [Back-filled from strategy_outlook bundle.]
- Working capital intensity has roughly doubled — 'In order to sustain business in this environment the Working Capital requirement has almost doubled.' Higher sulphur prices plus deliberately increased inventory levels lift capital employed and can offset the benefit of the Company's deleveraging, since the same disclosure sits alongside a stated shift to sourcing at a premium. [Back-filled from strategy_outlook bundle.]
- Export concentration and geopolitical / trade-policy exposure — Exports contributed 36% of revenue in FY26 and products are marketed in 22 countries. Export sales were adversely affected in FY26 by a weak global macro-economic and geopolitical environment, duties imposed by the USA, and the Iran-Israel war and its economic repercussions in the region. The Company states it had been absorbing part of the US tariff burden before the February 2026 tariff reduction. [Back-filled from profile / strategy_outlook bundles.]
- Sulphuric acid demand risk from fertilizer-sector production cuts — Elevated sulphur and other input prices are forcing fertilizer industries to cut production because the Government subsidy is not seen as enough to mitigate the cost increase, resulting in less demand for sulphuric acid. A subsidy revision is expected but not confirmed. This matters because the sulphuric acid and oleum business was the profit support in FY26 while insoluble sulphur margins compressed. [Back-filled from strategy_outlook bundle.]
- Single-product / single-end-market concentration in tyre chemicals — The Company's flagship product is insoluble sulphur sold principally into tyre manufacturing, and it describes itself as a dedicated platform for the Group's chemical business operating in one specialised global segment. The global insoluble sulphur market itself passed through 'one of its most testing phases in recent memory' driven by a sharp increase in global manufacturing capacities, muted tyre demand in select geographies and inventory overhangs across supply chains - a sector-wide overcapacity cycle to which the Company has no diversified offset beyond sulphuric acid. [Back-filled from profile bundle; stated as industry condition rather than under a 'Risks and Concerns' heading, which is absent from all six routed bundles.]
- Risk-management framework as disclosed is process-level, not a risk register — The only risk material actually routed into this bundle is the Directors' Report RISK MANAGEMENT paragraph: the Company has a risk management policy for risk identification, evaluation, assessment, mitigation and monitoring, with a demarcation of the roles of the Board and the Audit Committee; major risk elements 'have been identified and are being addressed systematically through mitigating action on a continuous basis'. No named risks or mitigations are listed, and the paragraph truncates mid-sentence at 'Audit Committee, under the'. No BRSR 'material responsible business conduct issues' table was routed into any of the six bundles.

business.body: OCCL is among a select group of global manufacturers with the capability to produce insoluble sulphur, a technically complex chemical used in tyre manufacturing and marketed under the premium brand Diamond Sulf; its products play a critical role in rubber vulcanisation, enhancing durability, heat resistance and performance stability. The Company supplies specialised chemical solutions to leading tyre and rubber manufacturers across global markets, with exports contributing 36% of revenue in FY26, and its products are marketed in 22 countries through a network of agents and strategically located warehouses. It also runs a sulphuric acid and oleum business, which the AR states delivered a strong performance in FY26 and supported overall profitability. The Company began in 1978 as Dharuhera Chemicals Limited producing sulphuric acid, entered insoluble sulphur in 1994, and today serves as the dedicated platform for the Group's chemical business, listed on BSE and NSE.

outlook.body:
- Secure raw-material (sulphur) availability from multiple sources, including at a premium where required, and hold higher inventory levels to ensure uninterrupted supply to customers amid the Gulf/Strait of Hormuz shortage
- Pass through raw-material and input-cost increases into selling prices to partially restore margins to sustainable levels
- Pursue trade remedies against Chinese import distortion: an anti-dumping duty absorption application was filed with the DGTR in March 2026, and an anti-absorption investigation has been initiated and is under review
- Strengthen the business structurally through the downcycle across technology, sustainability, customer engagement, cost competitiveness, supply-chain resilience, talent quality and Balance Sheet prudence (Chairman's statement, routed to the profile bundle)
- Lower the cost base and the break-even point of operations by enhancing process efficiencies, moderating energy consumption and questioning every cost element (Chairman's statement, routed to the profile bundle)
- Debottleneck existing capacities to extract higher throughput from existing assets rather than adding greenfield capacity (Operational review, routed to the profile bundle)
- Increase the share of renewable energy in the overall energy mix, as insoluble sulphur manufacturing is energy-intensive and energy competitiveness directly influences profitability (Chairman's statement / Operational review, routed to the profile bundle)
- Deepen engagement with global tyre manufacturers as a strategic long-term partner and expand customer plant approvals across geographies to widen wallet share (Chairman's statement, routed to the profile bundle)
- Strengthen product development capabilities, including development of future insoluble sulphur grades through the Company's pilot plant and co-development initiatives with leading global customers (Operational review / Intellectual capital, routed to the profile bundle)
- Develop advanced insoluble sulphur grades that help customers improve performance while reducing environmental impact, aligning with the tyre industry's shift to lower-carbon manufacturing (Chairman's statement, routed to the profile bundle)
- Preserve balance-sheet flexibility through debt prepayment and stronger liquidity (Chairman's statement, routed to the profile bundle)
- The AR does not set out a formal dividend-distribution policy in the routed text, but the stated intent is a resumption of regular cash returns alongside deleveraging. The Directors recommended a Final Dividend of Rs 1.80 per equity share of Rs 2 each (90%) for FY 2025-26 at the Board meeting of May 21, 2026, subject to shareholder approval at the 4th AGM to be held on August 27, 2026, in addition to an interim dividend already paid during the year (back-filled from the Directors' Report DIVIDEND section, routed to the strategy_outlook bundle; that section itself truncates mid-word at 'including interim divid', so the total-dividend-for-the-year figure could not be read). On the balance sheet, the Chairman states the Company prepaid debt, strengthened liquidity and preserved financial flexibility, so that it 'now has a stronger Balance Sheet and virtually no long-term debt', and the Operational review states that over the downcycle the Company repaid a substantial portion of its long-term debt and closed the year with a strengthened net worth. On reinvestment, the stated philosophy is capex-light: prospective growth 'can be serviced substantially through existing capacities... without corresponding by large capital expenditure', with spending directed at debottlenecking, renewable energy and product development rather than new greenfield capacity. Governance philosophy is stated as hinging on ethical practices, transparency and professional integrity, focused on long-term shareholder value growth. No buyback, credit rating or formal payout ratio is disclosed in the routed text. Rupee figures from the Directors' Report financial-results table and the KPI spread (revenue, EBITDA, net profit, RoCE, gearing) have deliberately NOT been reproduced here.
- Renewable energy: the Company commissioned renewable power capacities that generate electricity at a lower cost, described as a structural strengthening of competitiveness and environmental responsibility expected to endure; insoluble sulphur manufacturing is energy-intensive so energy competitiveness directly influences profitability. It has also been increasing the share of renewable energy in its overall energy mix. [Back-filled from Chairman's statement / Operational review, routed to the profile bundle.]
- Captive solar: the Company holds an investment in associate Clean Max Infinia Private Limited, established to leverage the Government of Haryana's captive solar power generation scheme for its Dharuhera plant; the associate had not commenced operations during the financial year ending March 31, 2026. [Back-filled from the Directors' Report.]
- Water: Dharuhera operations achieved water neutrality through groundwater recharge initiatives. [Back-filled from Chairman's statement.]
- Stated environmental focus areas: reducing emissions, optimising water consumption, enhancing access to renewable energy, lowering waste generation and moderating the carbon footprint, aligned with the global tyre industry's move toward lower-carbon and environmentally responsible manufacturing. [Back-filled from Chairman's statement.]
- Product-level sustainability: intensified development of advanced insoluble sulphur grades capable of helping customers enhance performance while reducing environmental impact, positioning OCCL with global customers who evaluate suppliers on sustainability alignment and not only price.
- External sustainability ratings and certifications: EcoVadis Gold Rating (among the top 5% of companies globally within its sector for sustainability performance) and Responsible Care Certification, both cited as reinforcing customer confidence in OCCL's environmental and governance standards; plus ISO 14001:2015 (Environment), ISO 45001:2018 (Occupational health and safety), ISO 20400:2017 (Sustainable procurement) and ISO 50001:2026 (Energy Management).
- CSR: the prescribed CSR expenditure for the year was not less than Rs 19.08 Lakh and the Company spent Rs 19.50 lakh on CSR activities during the year under review; the CSR Policy focus areas are Education, Health care and family welfare, Environment and Safety, and contributions to relief funds set up by the Government of India or any State Government. The CSR Committee comprises two Independent Directors (Mr. S. J. Khaitan as Chairman and Mr. H S Shashikumar) and one Executive Director (Mr. Arvind Goenka), and met once during the year on May 27, 2025.
- Social / human capital: as of March 31, 2026 the Company retained a workforce of 364 officers and workmen; a three-year wage settlement contract with workers was concluded amicably during the year; the Company invested in a younger, technically capable and multi-skilled workforce alongside re-skilling of experienced employees, and received the Excellence in Human Resources Award from the Indian Chemical Council. Community CSR continued around healthcare, education and community development near the manufacturing facilities.
- Governance: a Code of Conduct applies to Directors and senior management with affirmed compliance for FY26; 4 of 6 Board members are Independent Directors including one woman director; the Board met four times in FY26 with gaps within 120 days; a separate Independent Directors' meeting was held on March 23, 2026. No material pecuniary relationship exists between Independent Directors and the Company beyond sitting fees, expense reimbursement and annual commission.

outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: OCCL's expansion history is presented as a milestones timeline rather than as a forward capex plan. The Company was incorporated in 1978 as Dharuhera Chemicals Limited and commenced sulphuric acid production; it merged with Oriental Carbon Limited in 1984 to form Oriental Carbon & Chemicals Limited; and it commissioned the insoluble sulphur manufacturing facility in 1994, entering a specialised chemical segment. The 2000-2011 block records the divestment of the carbon black business to sharpen focus on specialty chemicals, the initiation of a greenfield investment at Mundra to establish a new insoluble sulphur manufacturing facility, and the commissioning of the first phase of the Mundra plant with 5,500 MTPA capacity. The 2012-2018 block records the second phase of the Mundra plant with an additional 5,500 MTPA capacity (2012), the initiation of a brownfield expansion programme in Mundra (2016), and the commissioning of the first (2017) and second (2018) phases of the Mundra expansion. The 2019-2022 block records the initiation of an additional 11,000 MTPA brownfield expansion at Dharuhera (2019), the commissioning of a 5,500 MTPA expansion at Dharuhera (2021), and the commissioning of additional sulphuric acid capacity (2022). Separately, the timeline carries a milestone that the Company 'Doubled its insoluble sulphur capacity following the commissioning of a second production line at Dharuhera'. FORWARD-LOOKING CAPEX: the AR discloses no new named expansion project with a commissioning or ramp timeline. On the contrary, the Chairman states that prospective growth can be serviced substantially through existing capacities without correspondingly large capital expenditure, and the Operational review describes the recent programme as debottlenecking of capacities to extract higher throughput from existing assets, increasing the share of renewable energy in the energy mix, strengthening product development capabilities (including a pilot plant for future insoluble sulphur grades), and co-development with leading global customers. The Company also commissioned renewable power capacities that generate electricity at a lower cost, and holds an investment in associate Clean Max Infinia Private Limited, established to leverage the Government of Haryana's captive solar power generation scheme for its Dharuhera plant (that associate had not commenced operations during the financial year ending March 31, 2026). outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- Insoluble sulphur market expected to remain highly volatile in 2026; Asia-Pacific continues to lead global demand, driven by robust manufacturing activity in China, India and South Korea
- India continues to be the fastest-growing market; GST rate cuts announced in September 2025 significantly boosted automobile sales, and April 2026 was the best-ever month for auto sales
- The reduction in US tariffs in February 2026 has positively impacted the Indian tyre industry and consequently OCCL's business; realisations are expected to improve as part of the tariff burden was previously being absorbed by the Company
- Supply-chain disruptions and rising sulphur prices have led Chinese manufacturers and other global suppliers to raise prices - previously a major obstacle to better realisations - and the Company was able to pass these increases on to customers and partially restore margins to sustainable levels, hence expects improved margins in FY 2026-27
- Demand from domestic tyre companies has seen an appreciable upturn in Q1 FY26-27 as import prices have increased and companies look to secure raw materials
- An anti-dumping duty absorption application filed with the DGTR for Chinese imports in March 2026, if implemented, is expected to further strengthen realisations
- Ongoing Middle East tensions and disruptions in the Strait of Hormuz have curtailed sulphur availability and disrupted shipping routes and logistics; nearly 45-50% of global sulphur exports originate from Gulf countries, leaving the industry highly vulnerable, and this has resulted in an 80%-100% rise in prices of sulphur and oil
- Energy, freight and insurance costs have risen sharply and are expected to adversely impact the business; working capital requirement has almost doubled to sustain business in this environment
- Historically high input costs may result in demand destruction, which could negatively affect sales volumes going forward
- Sulphuric acid: the Indian market is currently tight and bullish, driven by global sulphur shortages, with conditions more pronounced since March 2026 and a sharp increase in domestic prices; prices are expected to remain firm in the near term
- Sulphuric acid counter-driver: elevated sulphur and other input prices are forcing fertilizer industries to cut production because government subsidy is not seen as sufficient to mitigate the cost increase, reducing demand for sulphuric acid; the Government is looking into the matter and a revision is expected soon
- Structural demand driver cited from third-party sources: the global insoluble sulphur market was valued at USD 1.29 Billion in 2025 and is expected to reach USD 2.2 Billion by 2034, a CAGR of around 6.1%, with Asia Pacific accounting for over 56.25% of total demand
- Structural demand driver cited from third-party sources: shift toward premium and eco-friendly tyre formulations, with tyre OEMs adopting high-dispersion and low-oil (green) grades, and growth in EV-specific tyres
- Structural demand driver cited from third-party sources: India's replacement tyre segment accounted for nearly 58% of the total market in 2025, creating stable and recurring demand that insulates the industry when OEM vehicle sales slow

risks.note: Chinese manufacturers, burdened by excess capacities, directed surplus volumes into the Indian market at aggressive prices. An anti-dumping duty of USD 307 per tonne was imposed, but Chinese exporters absorbed the duty by lowering their selling prices ('anti-absorption'), negating the benefit available to domestic manufacturers. The Company applied for and the DGTR has initiated an anti-absorption investigation, and a further anti-dumping duty absorption application was filed in March 2026; both outcomes are pending, so the distortion is unresolved. As India's leading domestic insoluble sulphur manufacturer, OCCL states it 'bore the brunt of this'. [PROVENANCE: this bundle carried only the boilerplate Directors' Report risk-management-policy paragraph; the substantive risk content is back-filled from the Directors' Report OPERATIONS and FUTURE PROSPECTS sections and the Chairman's statement, which were routed to the profile and strategy_outlook bundles.]
risks.risk: Chinese import dumping and duty absorption in the Indian insoluble sulphur market

risks.note: Average sulphur cost rose from Rs 29 per kg to Rs 52 per kg during the year, reflecting geopolitical disruptions across global supply chains. Ongoing Middle East tensions and disruptions in the Strait of Hormuz have curtailed sulphur availability and disrupted shipping routes and logistics; nearly 45-50% of global sulphur exports originate from Gulf countries, so the industry remains highly vulnerable, and this has resulted in an 80%-100% rise in prices of sulphur and oil. The Company is securing raw materials from various sources, even at a premium, and has raised inventory. [Back-filled from profile / strategy_outlook bundles.]
risks.risk: Sulphur raw-material cost inflation and supply concentration in the Gulf

risks.note: Sulphur prices remained elevated while pricing flexibility in the insoluble sulphur market stayed constrained amid intense global competition, so cost pressures moved faster than realisations across parts of the market. Insoluble sulphur realisations could not increase in proportion to the rise in input costs, resulting in margin compression; profitability in FY26 was supported by the sulphuric acid business rather than the flagship product. Energy, freight and insurance costs have also risen sharply and are expected to adversely impact the business. [Back-filled from profile / strategy_outlook bundles.]
